context:
LumenAid is a fictional grants administrator integrating applicant organizations from its legacy CRM and a newly acquired regional registry. An entity is a legally registered organization; local chapters may be separate entities. CRM account numbers and registry numbers are different namespaces, although their string formats overlap. Registry records have a publication timestamp, but neither identifier reuse policy nor historical identifier validity has been established. Missing postal codes are much more common in the new registry, and transliterated names form a sizeable source-specific slice.

The existing additive scorer gives points for normalized name, address and identifier agreement. A dashboard labels its output “match probability,” despite no calibration study. Thresholds were selected using 900 analyst-reviewed pairs from last year's CRM-only candidate population. The candidate generator now adds a transliterated-name pass for registry rows; only 120 new-source reviews are affordable before the pilot. False merges can combine unrelated grant histories, while missed duplicates can produce duplicate award checks. Reviewers can abstain, and the pilot must remain shadow-only.

Recommend a scoring and review experiment with a credible simple baseline and at least one alternative. Explain source-aware evidence and missingness without assuming that either labels or source reliability transfer. State when a score can be interpreted probabilistically, what candidate changes do to that interpretation, and how to assess selection bias, slices and uncertainty. Keep evidence generation, threshold policy, resolution and legal-entity semantics separate; identify hard unknowns and reversible next steps.
title: LumenAid source-aware matching
